# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 70 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 70 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_070_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Part 1 — The Great Willow Tree

**70:1** He showed me a great willow tree overshadowing fields and mountains, and under the shadow of the willow all who were called by the name of the Lord had come together.

**70:2** And there stood an angel of the Lord, glorious and very tall, with a great sickle, and he was cutting branches from the willow and distributing them to those who sheltered under the tree. And he gave to them small rods, about a cubit in length.

**70:3** After all of them had received rods, the angel laid aside his sickle, and that tree appeared healthy, just as I had seen it before.

**70:4** And I marveled within myself and said: "How can the tree be healthy after so many branches were cut from it?" The shepherd said to me: "Do not marvel. The tree will remain healthy when all its branches have been pruned."

**70:5** "But why did some receive green branches, and others dry ones? And why were some completely withered and dry, while others had cracks, and others were green but had dried tips, and others were half-green and half-dry, and others were more dry than green, and still others were more green than dry, and others were covered with shoots, and still others had shoots with dried tips?"

**70:6** "Tell me, lord," I said, "what the varieties of rods mean, for I am troubled by these things." He answered me: "Listen and I will tell you the meaning of every rod."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the allegorical vision framework of Similitude 8.*
